summary: Closed T84#F-001 (readDefinitionDestination had no memoisation, making a found-then-failing `]:` quadratic: 6971ms in the detector at 200001 bytes and 6784-6952ms at all four public boundaries at 196610 bytes, with no attacker host in the payload) and T84#F-003 (indexContent's bracket pairing was blind to backslash escaping, so seven description-side spellings reached all four boundaries with redaction.state 'none' while marked fetched). T84#F-002, reference definitions inside container blocks, was NOT revisited: it is the user's accepted, documented limitation and all 17 of its rows still read BYPASS by design. The destination read is now memoised by its sticky offset, which changes no answer and makes total destination work provably linear because the whitespace runs at distinct `]:` offsets are pairwise disjoint. descriptionEnds now APPENDS two escape-aware candidate ends after the two escape-blind ones rather than replacing them, because replacing would delete the only candidate `![a\](URL)` has and exfil.ts:529-531 forbids moving in the release direction. Fuzzing found one real release the appending argument did not cover -- a new end grew a spurious link whose destination grammar swallowed the next line's genuine image -- so a construct that exists only through an escape-aware end is now flagged but never moves the scan cursor. With that guard the 28000-document differential fuzz reports zero span moves and zero host releases.
